newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: New offers at WTO telecoms talks encouraging.
newsitem.headline: New offers at WTO telecoms talks encouraging.

text.p: Ten countries submitted new or revised offers on Friday for a global pact on liberalising telecommunications markets which faces a Feb. 15 deadline, a top official said.

This brought to 54 the number of countries which have filed offers, with 14 new or revised offers expected next week, according to Neil McMillan, the British official who chairs the negotiating group of the World Trade Organisation (WTO).
"We've actually had not a bad harvest of new offers," McMillan told a news briefing after the one-day, closed talks. "Overall, I can say we are very encouraged..."
The telecommunications negotiations, part of the leftover business from the Uruguay Round which ended in December 1993, aim to break down barriers in the $600 billion world market.
The talks failed to meet a deadline of last April after the United States said offers from emerging economies were not good enough for it to open its domestic market to foreign operators.

The European Union also provided technical details on its offer of last November making clear that it covers transport of any signals -- including of sound, data or image -- but not the content or separate commercial activity, trade sources said.
EU negotiators said that the long-running WTO talks were "on track" for a successful conclusion in two weeks.
